# jcs

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/codec/jcs"
```

Package jcs writes the JSON Canonicalization Scheme of RFC 8785: one byte form for a JSON document — members sorted, no whitespace, numbers and strings spelled one way — so it can be signed or hashed, and checked by anyone who canonicalizes the same document.

```
canonical, err := jcs.Canonicalize(document)
digest := sha256.Sum256(canonical)
```

Marshal canonicalizes a Go value's encoding/json/v2 encoding. The document must be one I-JSON value (RFC 7493) — valid UTF-8, no duplicated member name — or Canonicalize returns [NotJSON](#NotJSON), naming the offset and never a byte of the document; a number past the largest finite double is [NumberInvalid](#NumberInvalid). It is not a codec Format: a canonical form is a policy over JSON, as strictjson is a policy over decoding.
